items.title: Ukraine, Russia alert apps hacked with fake nuclear alerts
items.summary: The breaches came overnight as the war's longest truce, around Oleshky in Kherson, ended; both governments said core warning systems kept working.

items.description: Both breaches came as a local ceasefire around the Russian-held town of Oleshky in the Kherson region came to an end. It was the longest truce of the war so far. The ceasefire started on Tuesday and ended on Sunday, Al Jazeera reported. According to Kyiv, the truce ended after Russia turned down an offer to extend it, Euronews reported.
items.bullet_summary_preload:
- Ukraine's **Air Alert** app falsely warned of nuclear and chemical threats and an **Oreshnik** missile launch late Sunday, Al Jazeera reported[1].
- Hours later, **Russia's Emergencies Ministry** said a "massive cyberattack" sent users fake warnings of nuclear warheads launched at every region, per AFP and Meduza[4][5].
- Kyiv blamed Moscow, while Ukrainian partisan group **Atesh** claimed the Russian hack; the attacks coincided with the end of the Oleshky truce in **Kherson**[2][9].
